title: 1973 AHSME Problem 25
statement: A circular grass plot \(12\) feet in diameter is cut by a straight gravel path \(3\) feet wide, one edge of which passes through the center of the plot. The number of square feet in the remaining grass area is

solutions.text:
The plot has radius \(6.\) At the path’s other edge, the perpendicular distance from the center is \(3,\) so the radius to an intersection point makes a \(30^\circ\) angle with the edge through the center. Half of the path consists of a \(30^\circ\) sector of radius \(6\) and a right triangle with legs \(3\) and \(3\sqrt3.\) Its area is \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{30}{360}\pi(6^2) +\frac12(3)(3\sqrt3)\\ &\qquad=3\pi+\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}. \end{aligned} \] Thus the whole path has area \(6\pi+9\sqrt3,\) and the remaining grass area is \[ 36\pi-(6\pi+9\sqrt3) =30\pi-9\sqrt3. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Bisect the path by the perpendicular diameter of the circular plot
Each half of the path is a \(30^\circ\) sector together with a \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle
